title: EEBench tests whether AI-designed circuits survive real constraints
friendlyTitle: A benchmark checks whether AI circuits actually work
summary: EEBench evaluates AI agents on circuit-design tasks using deterministic builds, SPICE simulations, component tolerances, availability and cost rather than judging whether a schematic merely looks plausible. Its current 13-task benchmark covers simulated analog and digital design, not physical layout or manufacturing.
friendlySummary: EEBench asks AI to design circuits, then tests voltage, timing, part limits and cost in simulations. It does not yet test building a complete physical board.
whyItMatters: Engineering agents need feedback tied to physical behaviour and trade-offs, not confident prose or attractive diagrams. Simulation-backed tests can help teams measure where AI assists real design work and where human review remains essential before anything reaches hardware.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A circuit that looks correct can still fail. Clear engineering tests help people use AI safely without trusting a design just because it sounds convincing.
